text: Choosing hundred dollar bills here costs the average guy two hundred grand.
A stranger offers you two piles of cash. Keep one.
Pile one is your weight in twenty dollar bills.
Pile two is hundred dollar bills, stacked flat, as tall as you.
A hundred is five twenties, so hundreds win easy, right?
Hit like if that's your pile.
But wait. Every bill weighs the same, about one gram.
So a pound of twenties is about nine thousand dollars.
And one inch of hundreds is about twenty-three thousand.
Send this to the friend who'd grab hundreds without— without blinking.
But here's the catch: you've got way more pounds than inches.
Per the CDC, the average American man weighs one ninety-nine pounds.
But he's only sixty-nine inches tall.
So it's one ninety-nine pounds of twenties against sixty-nine inches of hundreds.
So his height in hundreds is about one point six million.
His weight's next, and it's worth a follow.
His weight in twenties is about one point eight million.
The small bills win by two hundred grand.
That's a hundred bucks a day for over five years.
Still choosing the hundred dollar bills?
